long_biography.plain_text:
During Armen Hovnanian's childhood, his father Hirair left engineering, bought New Jersey land and created a homebuilding company around single-family communities for retirees. Hovsons expanded from 74 homes in its first year into developments across New Jersey, Florida and California, then added medical facilities, shopping centres, offices and apartments. Armen entered that organisation with his sister Edele by 1994.

His assignments later spanned Menk Corporation, Hovchild Partnership, Hovsons and Hovnanian Property Management, where he was consistently identified as a developer. Hovchild held enough land to rank as Berkeley Township's largest property taxpayer, while Hovsons came to manage millions of square feet of commercial premises. In 2012, he remained affiliated with the group's property-management arm and described his occupation as real estate.
